title: Manual prior
description: A game prior derived from the boxed manual and from on-screen scans. Manual facts carry page citations and name concepts; scan facts name realisations (types, hit points, addresses). The two layers stay separate so a concept is never confused with its implementation.

schema_version.description: 1 = legacy flat file (notes/templates/target_types/...). 2 = concept layer plus realisation layer. Both are readable by the planner; 2 is what the parse pipeline emits.

source.description: Where the manual comes from: scan id / archive.org id / file name. Must name a scan a person can open, not a recollection.

notes.description: Free-text route notes kept for humans and for the planner's log. Legacy field.

manual.description: Provenance of the document the facts were read from.

scan_id.description: Archive item or file name of the PDF, as in docs/manuals.md.

language.description: Language of the scan actually parsed.

pages_used.description: Pages the parse read. Empty is honest; it means the whole document was fed without page selection.

parse.description: How the PDF became facts. Filled by the pipeline, not by hand.

judge.description: Who corrected the machine output, if anyone. Corrections are logged; the judge does not invent facts.

judge_log.description: Path to the correction log, relative to the repository root.

facts.description: Concept-layer statements from the manual. Every fact needs a citation. Realisation values do not belong here.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. destroy-sensor, fire-left, door-up.

kind.description: Ontology slot. game-agnostic: collectible=thing to pick up, ability=jump/duck/throw/pick, target=thing to destroy, goal=win condition, exit=way on, health/lives go under hud or hazard as fits.

statement.description: What the manual says, in one sentence. No numbers that come from RAM.

scope.description: When the fact applies. Prefer the manual's own axes (scroll mode, area) over invented splits.

axis.description: e.g. scroll_mode, area, screen, menu, any

value.description: e.g. horizontal, vertical, 3d, underwater, base, jungle, title

why.description: Why this scope, citing the page that scopes it.

page.description: Page in the scan. Required: a fact without a page is not a fact.

quote.description: Short quote or caption from the page. Original language is fine; translation goes in statement.

figure.description: Figure or illustration id if the fact comes from a picture rather than text.

status.description: extracted = machine only; human_confirmed = a judge agreed; rejected = a judge struck it (keep the row, do not delete).

goal.description: What the game wants done, in manual words.

player.description: Who the player is and what they can do.

controls.description: The manual's control table. Button meanings as words; whether fire is tap or hold is a scan question, not a manual one.

notes.description: e.g. on 3D screens the gun points forward only

targets.description: Split layer: what the manual calls a target, and how the scan realises it. Keep them apart.

concepts.description: Manual words for things worth destroying or collecting.

realisation.description: SCAN-DERIVED. Object type ids, hit points, pricing. Never hand-written from the manual; the manual only names concepts.

types.description: Object type ids from object_tables.py for the concepts above.

target_px.description: Pixels of progress per hit point. From the stage stride arithmetic, or the generic floor rule.

found_by.description: Which scan produced this, e.g. object_tables.py at commit …

exit.description: Where the way on is, in manual words. Coordinates are realisation and go in realisation.

way_on.description: e.g. upward through the door in the middle of the far wall

realisation.description: SCAN-DERIVED route numbers the planner prices, e.g. exit_up_px, exit_at_x.

statement.description: e.g. a cleared stage grants an extra life

templates.description: Button sequences the planner may try. Those that come from the manual's control table need a citation; those from controllability.py name found_by.

tables.description: SCAN-DERIVED RAM layout for object types and hit points. Forbidden in a held-out prior unless produced by object_tables.py.

scope.description: Legacy planner scope: when the stage-specific half of the prior applies. Prefer facts[].scope; this stays while oracle_mpc.py reads it.

target_types.description: Legacy flat realisation of targets.concepts. Kept so oracle_mpc.py runs unchanged; prefer targets.realisation.types.
